_doc: Ship gates for a video-route character (scripts/assets/cast_walk.py gate). Every gate must PASS. Thresholds are the frog-settler's accepted numbers (CURATION.md, 2026-09-25), not taste.
_seam: loop seam / ordinary frame step, per direction. The frog shipped 0.16-0.48.
_seam_max_dir: Aaron's decision, 2026-09-29: n (the back view) gets 1.0; every other direction keeps 0.5. The mycologist's three n takes measured 0.56 / 0.79 / 0.91 against 0.5.
_seam_exception: Per-kind, testing only, flagged for a redo in both CURATION.md. mireclaw-stalker: Aaron, 2026-09-29 09:3x, 'Let's use what we have for now. The earlier stalker animations were pretty good, except for a flash near his feet, and possibly the loop.' Eight legs step at independent phases, so Wan I2V gives no loop point under 0.5 (best single-frame seams across 3 takes: s .48 off-model, se 1.32, ne 1.15). Ceilings are the shipped loops' measured seams rounded up to 0.1: s 1.564 (take2 P25), se 1.341 (take2 P24), e .566 (take1 P24), ne 1.31 (take2 P24); n .983 is under n's 1.0. Unpark path: the rotoscope rig (QUEUE.md).

colour._: share of a direction's opaque pixels (all 10 frames) in colours that are >= min_share of the direction and farther than far_rgb from every colour making up >= anchor_share of the s-idle. The frog measures 0.005 at worst, the shipped vine-ranger 0.009; the mycologist's cyan e-visor measured 0.030.

consistency: consistency.py <kind> --check exits 0 (silhouette spec in consistency-spec.json, 48 px pack)

verify.frames: every frame, job = its direction's idle: s/se face visible, e a profile, ne/n no face

judge._: sprites.judge (judge-sprite-mp4) on each direction's raw loop. identity_drift, sharpness and coverage_jitter keep sprites.judge.GATES. Those GATES were calibrated on a Blender mannequin render and 40 fps boil clips; on 16 fps Wan walks the approved frog failed them (flicker 11.7-19.2 vs 5 in 5/5 directions, head_drift .066-.134 vs .08), and flicker cannot see boil there (heavy synthetic boil moved the mycologist's e from 22.3 to 24.3). So flicker is replaced by boil and head_drift is set from the frog. cast_gate_selftest.py proves both ways.
judge._boil: cast_walk.boil: motion-compensated frame residual / in-silhouette contrast, the loop resampled to 16 frames per stride. The frog's shipped loops measure .103-.282; the judge's rejected boil clips (sporefall-art wip/demos/hifps, at 16 fps) measure far above. The near-still idle reject stays under every metric here.
judge._head_drift: the frog's shipped loops .066-.134; the rejected boil clips .41-.75

style._: verify.py --style --kind against the frog: rendering only (pixel density, outline, flat lighting), not colour; colour is gate 2 and the palette gate

palette._: share of opaque pixels whose colour is not one of palette.py's locked 34. Export snaps every frame onto the s-idle's colours; the frog and the mycologist measure 0. Replaces the style prompt's colour question, which described the palette as teal/olive and failed a cream suit drawn entirely in the locked colours.
